newsitem.title: UK: Lithuania c.banker sees Eurobond this year.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania c.banker sees Eurobond this year.

text.p: Lithuania aims to issue a $200 million Eurobond later this year but the plans will depend on the state of the Eurodollar market and a new credit rating, central bank deputy head Jonas Niaura said on Saturday.
The Baltic state has already issued two Eurobonds, for $60 million and $50 million, and has mandated JP Morgan Securities to lead the new issue.
Lithuania is awaiting a credit rating from Standard & Poor's before going ahead. It already has a rating of Ba2 from Moody's Investors Service.

"Depending on the results of the Standard & Poor's rating and the general development in the Eurodollar market, Lithuania is going to issue the bond later in 1997," Niaura told a Euromoney conference.
He said Lithuania had borrowed $1.4 billion since 1990 and had repaid $224 million.
